🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin cooled to $79K after a 23% week, but the money kept arriving — August ETF inflows topped $3 billion. Meanwhile Tokyo, Frankfurt and Dallas all moved on tokenization on the same day. 📉 Bitcoin Takes a Breather at $79K After a 23% Week Bitcoin slipped back toward $79,000 on Wednesday after briefly clearing $81,000, ending a seven-day run that added roughly 23%. Around $566 million in positions were liquidated over 24 hours — about $331 million of it shorts — confirming how much of the breakout was short covering rather than fresh conviction. Ether, Solana and XRP all gave back ground as traders banked the week's gains. Read full story 🏦 Spot Bitcoin ETFs Push August Inflows Past $3 Billion US spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their inflow streak to a seventh straight trading day on Tuesday with $314.37 million added, lifting August's total to $3.03 billion — now within $390 million of October 2025's record with four sessions left. Total net assets reached $99.05 billion, and the rebound has cut year-to-date net outflows by more than half to $2.26 billion. More details 🧮 Strategy Cuts Net Leverage to Near Zero Michael Saylor's bitcoin treasury company has brought its cash position almost level with its convertible debt, effectively neutralising net leverage. Strategy has also built close to four years of coverage for its preferred dividends while continuing to buy back STRC below par — a defensive posture that reshapes the risk profile of the largest corporate BTC holder. Read more ⚠️ Dallas Fed Warns Tokenized Deposits Could Strip $700B From Bank Lending A new Dallas Fed analysis argues that programmable deposits combined with AI agents could let customers switch banks instantly and automatically in pursuit of higher yields. The paper estimates the resulting funding-cost pressure could remove around $700 billion of lending capacity from the US banking system — the sharpest official warning yet on tokenized deposits. See details 🇯🇵 Japan Starts Building Tokenized Stock and Bond Settlement Japan's FSA, Finance Ministry, Bank of Japan and major financial institutions will begin work this year on a blockchain settlement network for equities and government bonds. This partnership underscores the increasing integration of stablecoins into the legacy financial system. See details 🏦JPMorgan weighs stablecoin launch as Wells Fargo and banks advance joint venture JPMorgan is exploring the launch of its own stablecoin as part of an evolving deposit token strategy. These changes aim to modernize how investment advisers safeguard digital assets under federal law.
